- Use `chown` to assign ownership: `sudo chown user:group /path/to/executable` (sets owner and group).
- Use `chmod` to set permissions: `sudo chmod 750 /path/to/executable` (owner has read, write, execute; group has read and execute; others have none).
- Use `setfacl` for fine-grained control: `sudo setfacl -m u:username:r-x /path/to/executable` (allows specific user to read and execute).
- Verify permissions with `ls -l /path/to/executable` and `getfacl /path/to/executable`.
- Test execution with `./path/to/executable` (ensure it runs only for authorized users).
